title: Cost per active student per month

metrics.reason: config/sage-budget.json.monthlyBudgetUsd ships null on purpose (a guessed ceiling would let a real overrun read as 'under budget'), and even once Britt sets it the floor is budget/activeStudents — a number that moves with enrollment, not a fixed value this config can hold. The scorer computes the would-be floor and VisionQuest's existing budgetCheck verdict (ok/warning/no_price/no_budget) into metrics[0].details on every run regardless.

A raw descriptive count with no correctness bar of its own — the thing that should be floored is the FERPA routing RATIO, which the sibling ferpa-routing suite already covers. This number exists so a reader can see the denominator behind that ratio.
Same as cloud_calls_total: a descriptive count, not a metric with its own floor.

notes: Reuses scripts/sage-ai-accountability.mjs's buildProviderMix()/buildCostReport() (this session added exports for both, no CLI behavior change) over the trailing 30 days from AuditLog(targetType="ai_request") and LlmCallLog, connected via BENCH_PROD_READONLY_URL rather than the script's own DATABASE_URL default. 'Active student' = distinct LlmCallLog.studentId in the window (an aggregate count only; no student id is ever logged or included in output). displayUnit:"usd" on usd_per_active_student_month is a pass-through hint for the dashboard — the contract's unit enum (ratio|percent|count|ms|grade|seconds) has no currency type, so unit stays "count" and this says what the count actually means.
